title: The export path now derives the kernel-section offset and the nchw geometry, and 1x896 is exact through the real runtime
verdict: Both export-path residuals named in receipts/2026-09-14-1x896-channel-polarity.json are fixed in source, derived from the artifacts rather than stamped from a convention, and proven on device. The coefficient stream comes from the weight blob's own declared payload offset instead of byte 0 of the blob file, and the nchw plane and row bytes come from the task's own tile-DMA byte counts instead of the 64-byte-padded convention. Three guarded single-iteration executes on jwm1: the device-qualified 64-element control, the re-exported 1x512 and the re-exported 1x896 all returned exact, status 0, 6 ms wall each. The 64-element class is untouched, by construction and by measurement.

derivation_1_kernel_section_offset.defect: For a MIL BLOBFILE constant, __TEXT,__const carries the CoreML weight blob FILE from byte 0. The converter copied that section through, so the engine read the blob's 0x40 header plus its 0x40 0xDEADBEEF record as the first 64 fp16 coefficients and lost the last 64 real ones.
derivation_1_kernel_section_offset.fix: kernel_payload() sources the section from the blob payload. blob_payload_offset() walks the blob's 0x40-byte metadata records from 0x40, and for the record whose declared byte count equals krn_size returns the payload offset the record itself states. Every candidate is checked against the record end and the file length, and a blob that does not name exactly one matching payload is an error.
derivation_1_kernel_section_offset.why_it_is_not_a_constant: The MIL declares BLOBFILE(offset = uint64(64)) and the writer adds a further 0x40 record, so 0x80 is the sum of two independent facts, not a format constant. Both retained blobs state 0x80 in their record; the converter reads it.
derivation_1_kernel_section_offset.new_input: --weights PATH. A blob-backed object cannot be converted without it: the HWX embeds only weights.bin[0 : krn_size], so the real coefficient tail is not in the object at all. Measured on the 1x512 HWX: __TEXT,__const is byte-identical to weights.bin[0x0:0x400] and the remaining 0x80 bytes of payload are absent, the segment past the section being zero. The converter therefore refuses rather than emitting a truncated, header-prefixed coefficient stream.
derivation_1_kernel_section_offset.verified_offline: For the 1x512 and 1x896 objects the emitted section equals weights.bin[0x80 : 0x80+krn_size] exactly, and reads as one distinct fp16 value, 0.25, repeated 512 and 896 times. The shipped artifacts instead carry 8 distinct values including -427.25 and -1.733, the blob header decoded as fp16.

derivation_2_header_geometry.defect: The exported header declared nchw[4] = nchw[5] = (1,C,1,1,64,64), the 64-byte-padded plane convention, while the task's own tile DMA was configured for a dense surface. mlx-omarchy packs at the nchw plane stride, so the host scattered input across 64-byte rows the engine never read.
derivation_2_header_geometry.fix: derive_strides(shape, total, run) reads the task's whole-surface and contiguous-run byte counts and takes their ratio as the row count. One run per channel is the padded plane layout and the run stride is the plane stride; a single run is a dense surface whose plane stride is the surface divided among its channels. Counts the task does not account for fall back to the padding convention, which is never a new guess.

registers.walk: count-1 in bits 26..31 of a record header, register byte address in bits 0..25. A record running past the descriptor is now an error, which is the -110 defect class rather than a partial decode.

measured_per_program.note: unchanged; rows equals the channel count, so the padded reading is the derived one
unchanged; 3 runs against 4 declared channels is unaccounted, so the convention stands

derivation_2_header_geometry.tile_consequence: tiles[4] and tiles[5] follow the derived plane stride, so a dense 1792-byte surface now declares 1 tile (16384 bytes) instead of 4 (65536). This is the one field where the converter output differs from the hand-corrected artifact proven on 2026-09-14, and it is the truthful allocation: libane stages tiles[channel] * 0x4000 per channel (mlx-omarchy docs/ane-bundles.md:93-94). It was exercised on device below.

also_added.kernel_placement_invariant: parse_hwx now rejects a kernel section that is not at align16(tsk_size). libane locates the section there, so a section anywhere else is read from the wrong bytes whatever it holds. It holds for every object inspected, including the two retained Qwen production exports (tsk 0xea2f8 with kernel at 0xea300, and 0xc36f8 with 0xc3700).

device.libane: the derived-channel build from omarchy-ane ane-parity 20d24ad, /var/tmp/AneChannelPolarity-20260914/libane-polarity.so sha256 bf4dbe5482d9eefd137108b88c3cb807f8cf3fdb32e02d6ed5314fea52201d95, loaded with --libane. The exported family needs it: its task puts the destination on channel 5 and the source on channel 4, the reverse of the positional layout. The commit is the pin; the digest is a consequence of the toolchain. I wrote that a matching digest across two hosts would be the surprising result and I was wrong: T6001ExportFamily rebuilt from the same commit with jw16's gcc 16.1.1 20260430 and got bf4dbe54... byte-identical, same distribution and compiler version giving reproducible output. So the digest is reproducible under an identical toolchain rather than host-specific, and it can be compared directly when the toolchains match.
device.libane_cannot_be_identified_by_symbol: nm cannot distinguish the derived build from a positional one: the whole derivation is static inline in libane/ane_bind.h and exports no symbol, so ane_bind_init does not appear. Identify it by source digest plus the behavioural argument -- with a positional binding this exported family completes and returns a wrong element 0, so an exact result is itself proof the derived map took effect. Established by T6001ExportFamily, who planned the nm check and found it useless.
device.libane_pin_is_userspace_only: This pin means the libane sources at 20d24ad, NOT the branch wholesale. Verified read-only in the local omarchy-ane checkout: 8554583 (main, 'ane: T6001 bind and SET genpd; document SoC coverage') is not an ancestor of 20d24ad, and it is the one main commit ane-parity lacks. Against their merge-base b66ca80f, ane-parity changes only userspace (libane/ane.c, libane/ane.h, libane/ane_bind.h, test/bind) while main changes only the kernel module (ane/src/ane_drv.c 929 lines, ane/src/ane.h, ane/src/ane_tm.c, plus ane/t6001-j316c-set-domains.dts which ane-parity does not have at all). So ane-parity is libane-complete and NOT T6001-complete: building the kernel module from it would lose main's T6001 bind and SET genpd work. Harmless for this receipt and for T6001ExportFamily's reproduction because neither rebuilt the module, and ane/src/uapi/drm/ane_accel.h is byte-identical between the two commits (empty diff), so the userspace ABI is the same object either way. Raised by T6001ExportFamily and confirmed here independently.

results.exact_means_value_equal_not_byte_equal: The worker compares fp16 VALUES, not bytes: tools/mlx-omarchy-ane-worker/main.cpp:44-55 fp16_values_equal walks 16-bit lanes, accepts a lane where both sides are zero regardless of sign ((left & 0x7FFF) == 0 && (right & 0x7FFF) == 0), and is otherwise a bit compare -- so for non-zero lanes value-equality IS bit-equality. It matters for this control and only this control: T6001ExportFamily measured the device-written y on jw16 at sha256 bade941d against the expected y.bin abd3b8c9, differing in exactly 5 of 128 bytes at fp16 slots 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31, where the expected file holds 0x8000 (-0.0) and the device wrote 0x0000 (+0.0). Zero differing values, five differing bytes. Same signed-zero behaviour already recorded in mlx-omarchy receipts/2026-09-13-jw16-ane-set-exec.json. The precise statement for the control on BOTH hosts is value-equal, not byte-equal. The two re-exports are unaffected: their expected output is 1.25 in every lane, so no zero exists for the tolerance to act on and value-equality is byte-equality there. Narrowing supplied by T6001ExportFamily against a loose 'byte-identical' claim of mine.

derive_strides covers a [1,C,H,W] fp16 surface. A program whose rows are neither one-per-channel nor a single contiguous run falls back to the padding convention, which is right for the two in-repo samples but is a fallback, not a derivation. A multi-run padded surface with H > 1 has not been observed and is untested on device.

Neither host saved the produced output. The worker has --save NAME=FILE (main.cpp:111) beside --expect and neither runner used it, so no y digest exists for the 1x512 or 1x896 on either host: the cross-SoC output equality runs transitively through byte-identical expected files under fp16 value comparison. That is sound but weaker than two hashes of two produced buffers. Fix is one flag on both hosts; not worth a re-submit on its own, and a one-host digest would have no counterpart to compare against. Raised by T6001ExportFamily.

fp16_values_equal skips a trailing odd byte (its loop runs i + 1 < size), so an odd-length output buffer's last byte is never compared. Inert for everything submitted here -- 128, 1024 and 1792 bytes are all even -- but it is a hole in the comparator rather than a property of these runs.
